title: Will a Raise Push You Into a Higher Tax Bracket? (The Truth)
description:
Crossing into a higher tax bracket does not mean all of your income gets taxed at the higher rate. Using a stickman and a row of tax buckets, this video explains how U.S. federal income tax brackets really work, with official IRS figures for tax year 2027: a $1,000 raise that crosses the 22% line adds about $167.50 in federal income tax, and the effective rate stays around 11.6%, not 22%.

In this video:
- Hook: the coworker who says your raise will cost you
- The myth: one step up the staircase taxes everything
- The standard deduction: the tax-free bucket that fills first
- How brackets actually work: income as water poured into buckets
- Worked example: a $1,000 raise across the 22% line
- Marginal vs. effective tax rate
- Why the buckets grow every year: inflation indexing (2026 vs. 2027)
- The honest exception: benefits cliffs
- What it means for you
- Conclusion

Sources:
